climbing_route.label: Final pitch to the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col
climbing_route.notes: Crampon up the final snow/scree pitch to the col itself. Once melted out late-season it turns to loose, chossy class 3-4 scrambling, with an overhanging boulder near the top sometimes forcing a chossy class 3/4 bypass on the left. The route text stops at the col.

climbing_route.label: Talus/scree to the Sawtooth crest
climbing_route.notes: From Middle Oval Lake's outflow, leave the maintained tread and scramble cross-country up open talus/scree slopes to the north/northeast to gain the Sawtooth crest at a broad saddle roughly 1,200-1,500 ft above the lake. No reliable water sources above the lake, so carry all you will need.

climbing_route.label: Crest north/northwest to the summit block
climbing_route.notes: Follow the rocky crest generally north/northwest over blocky, sometimes loose talus to Oval Peak's summit block. Class 2 but with real route-finding and loose-rock exposure in poor visibility.

climbing_route.label: Rock ledges to the southwest ridge
climbing_route.notes: From 3,100 ft where the maintained tread ends, climb a short but steep ~70-foot band of rock ledges covered in dirt and moss to gain the southwest ridge. The crux of the lower route — insecure, especially if wet.

climbing_route.label: Southwest ridge crest to the Ruby Lake overlook
climbing_route.notes: Above the ledges the path thins to an intermittent boot track marked intermittently with old pink flagging; stay on the crest/southwest side of the ridge through open, flower-strewn meadows. Around 5,800 ft the visible path effectively disappears at an overlook above Ruby Lake — the key route-finding checkpoint.

climbing_route.label: Steepening ground to the stunted trees at 6,700 ft
climbing_route.notes: From the overlook the line continues up steepening terrain, ~300 ft of gain, staying on the right (west) side of the ridge crest, to about 6,700 ft where you squeeze through a last band of stunted trees, again flagged with pink ribbon.

climbing_route.label: Final scree and blocky rock to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Above the trees there is no more ground cover; the final several hundred feet to the 6,975-ft summit — site of an old, collapsed fire lookout — is loose scree and blocky rock. Loose rock and scree-on-slab underfoot are the main hazards throughout the upper ridge, along with route-finding in fog since the flagging is sparse and the path is not maintained.

climbing_route.label: Challenger Glacier to the summit rock pitch
climbing_route.notes: The final push crosses the crevassed Challenger Glacier to a short summit rock pitch. Remote and weather-exposed, with essentially no bailout options once committed.

climbing_route.label: Notch at the McAllister-Klawatti col
climbing_route.notes: From Klawatti Col camp the climb of Primus itself is a summit-day push: down-climb or make a short (~50 ft) rappel through the notch at the McAllister-Klawatti col onto the North Klawatti Glacier.

climbing_route.label: North Klawatti Glacier to the base of the south/west ridge
climbing_route.notes: Rope up and traverse east/north across the glacier to the base of Primus's south/west ridge, probing for hidden crevasses — this section has caught parties by surprise even in good visibility.

climbing_route.label: Snow-covered talus to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Unrope and scramble snow-covered talus to the 8,508 ft summit.

climbing_route.label: Boot path up the west slope
climbing_route.notes: From the cairn planted in the middle of the path near the tarn, pick up a boot path climbing the west slope. The track is intermittent and easy to lose on scree, so stay close to the ridge crest on climber's right (south) if you're unsure of the line.

climbing_route.label: Final 900 ft of red rock and scree
climbing_route.notes: The final roughly 900 ft over the last half mile is a 30-40° slope of fractured red (iron-stained) rock, loose scree, heather, and scattered alpine trees, with no real exposure — hands are needed intermittently but it's non-technical. This upper slope holds snow into early summer and can present avalanche/glissade hazard in spring conditions; by mid-to-late summer it's typically dry but still loose and slick when wet.

wa_ridge_traverse_from_east_fury.skip_reason: The approach text is the generic Ross Dam / Ross Lake water taxi / Big Beaver valley / Beaver Pass / Challenger Glacier expedition description, shared verbatim with wa_poltergeist_pinnacle. It describes no ridge traverse from East Fury and no climbing on this route — re-homing the Challenger Glacier summit pitch here would attach another peak's beta to this route.

climbing_route.label: Ruth's summit, then descent to the Ruth-Icy saddle
climbing_route.notes: Done conventionally Ruth-to-Icy: tag Ruth's summit first, then descend roughly 800 ft south and west toward a gully on the peak's west side, pick up a faint boot path, and continue down another ~800 ft (about 1,600 ft total off Ruth's summit) to the low saddle/col between Ruth and Icy at roughly 6,600-6,800 ft. Parties choose between a steeper, more direct 'death gully' line or supposedly-cairned heather slopes and game trails to climber's left holding 2nd-3rd class ground — the heather-slope option is the safer, recommended line.

climbing_route.label: Connecting ridge to the Icy Glacier
climbing_route.notes: From the saddle, cross a patch of trees and talus/boot-path along the connecting ridge to the Icy Glacier, then ascend talus and slabs below a rock ridge to gain the glacier proper, aiming for a notch/saddle just west of Icy's Northwest Spire (~6,500 ft).

climbing_route.label: Light-colored gully system to the summit block
climbing_route.notes: From that notch it's another ~500 ft of scrambling up an obvious left-hand, light-colored gully system to the base of Icy's summit block.

climbing_route.label: Summit gully to the top
climbing_route.notes: A 100-ft gully of solid jugs and ledges but real exposure leads to the top. Helmets are standard here given loose rock and traffic funneled through a single gully. The true (highest) summit is the SE point, about 11 ft higher than the peak most maps label as the top.
